problems.quote: Passed by British Parliament on July 18, 1947.
problems.problem: The Indian Independence Act was passed by Parliament on July 15, 1947; July 18 was the date of royal assent.
problems.correction: Passed by British Parliament on July 15, 1947.
problems.verifierReason: Indian Independence Act passed by Parliament 15 July 1947; 18 July was royal assent.

problems.quote: The colony at Shortughai (Amu Darya, Afghanistan, c. 2500 BCE, 2000 km from Indus)
problems.problem: Shortughai is dated to c. 2000 BCE, not 2500 BCE.
problems.correction: The colony at Shortughai (Amu Darya, Afghanistan, c. 2000 BCE, 2000 km from Indus)
problems.verifierReason: Shortughai is a Mature Harappan trading outpost dated to c. 2000 BCE, not 2500 BCE.

problems.quote: Ten Indus signs across the top.
problems.problem: The Pashupati seal bears seven signs, not ten.
problems.correction: Seven Indus signs across the top.
problems.verifierReason: The Pashupati seal (Mohenjo-daro 420) bears seven signs in its top register, not ten.

problems.quote: The Dholavira signboard shows boustrophedon (alternating direction per line, like ox-ploughing).
problems.problem: The Dholavira signboard is a single-line inscription; it does not exhibit boustrophedon.
problems.correction: The Dholavira signboard is a single-line inscription written right-to-left.
problems.verifierReason: The Dholavira signboard is a single-line, right-to-left inscription of ten signs; it has no second line to show boustrophedon.

problems.quote: If CAT → DDU, then how is DOG coded? (Each letter +1: D→E, O→P, G→H → EPH)
problems.problem: The example CAT→DDU does not follow a fixed shift of +1 (C→D is +1, A→D is +3, T→U is +1), yet the solution for DOG assumes a uniform +1 shift. This contradicts the rule 'Each letter is shifted forward or backward by a fixed number of positions.'
problems.correction: If CAT → DBU (each letter +1), then DOG → EPH.
problems.verifierReason: Original puzzle has inconsistent example; correction aligns example with stated +1 shift rule.

problems.quote: and (for appointment of puisne judges) the Chief Minister
problems.problem: The Chief Minister is not part of the constitutional consultation process for High Court judge appointments under Article 217; consultation is with the CJI, the Chief Justice of the High Court, and the Governor.
problems.correction: consultation with the CJI, the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, and the Governor of the state
problems.verifierReason: Article 217 requires consultation with CJI, Governor, and Chief Justice of HC; Chief Minister has no constitutional role.

problems.quote: Introduced by the Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act 2005
problems.problem: The act that introduced plea bargaining is the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2005, not the Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act.
problems.correction: Introduced by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2005
problems.verifierReason: Plea bargaining was introduced by Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2005 (Act 2 of 2006), not Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act.

problems.quote: Applicable to offenses punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years (not affecting the socio-economic condition of society).
problems.problem: The exclusion is for offenses affecting the socio-economic condition of the country, not "not affecting".
problems.correction: Applicable to offenses punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years, except offenses affecting the socio-economic condition of the country
problems.verifierReason: Section 265A(2) CrPC excludes offences affecting socio-economic condition of the country; original misstates as 'society' and phrasing is ambiguous.

problems.quote: Remember that rotation is invertible only when s and L are coprime
problems.problem: Rotation (cyclic shift) is always invertible for any shift s; the condition for the permutation to be a single cycle is that s and L are coprime, not invertibility.
problems.correction: Remember that rotation forms a single cycle only when s and L are coprime
problems.verifierReason: Rotation is always invertible (inverse shift L-s). Coprime condition ensures single cycle, not invertibility.

problems.quote: Work Done is directly proportional to Efficiency and inversely proportional to Time.
problems.problem: Work Done is directly proportional to Time (Work = Efficiency × Time), not inversely proportional. The inverse proportionality holds between Time and Efficiency for a fixed amount of work.
problems.correction: Work Done is directly proportional to Efficiency and directly proportional to Time.
problems.verifierReason: Original quote incorrectly states Work ∝ 1/Time. Standard formula Work = Efficiency × Time shows direct proportionality to both (other variable constant). Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: during the Gupta period Xuanzang reported they constituted a majority of Indian Buddhists
problems.problem: Xuanzang visited India in the 7th century CE, not during the Gupta period (c. 320–550 CE).
problems.correction: by the 7th century CE, Xuanzang reported they constituted a majority of Indian Buddhists
problems.verifierReason: Xuanzang visited India 629–645 CE, post-Gupta; correction fixes the period accurately.

problems.quote: Fourth Council (c. 78-100 CE) : Two separate councils. Theravada : at Aloka Vihara, Sri Lanka (Patron: Vattagamani Abhaya) Pali Canon written on palm leaves for the first time
problems.problem: The Theravada council that wrote the Pali Canon occurred in the 1st century BCE (c. 29 BCE), not 78–100 CE. The date range applies only to the Sarvastivada council.
problems.correction: Fourth Council: Theravada (c. 29 BCE) at Aloka Vihara, Sri Lanka wrote the Pali Canon; Sarvastivada (c. 78-100 CE) at Kundalavana, Kashmir compiled the Mahavibhasha
problems.verifierReason: Theravada Fourth Council was c. 29 BCE in Sri Lanka; Sarvastivada was c. 78–100 CE in Kashmir. Correction separates them correctly.

problems.quote: 1 + R/100 = 10 log(A/P)/T (or e ... for natural logs), and finally R = 100(10 log(A/P)/T - 1)
problems.problem: The formula incorrectly uses multiplication by 10 (or e) instead of exponentiation. For base-10 logs, 1+R/100 = 10^{log(A/P)/T}; for natural logs, 1+R/100 = e^{ln(A/P)/T}.
problems.correction: 1 + R/100 = 10^{log(A/P)/T} (or e^{ln(A/P)/T} for natural logs), and finally R = 100(10^{log(A/P)/T} - 1)
problems.verifierReason: Original uses multiplication (10 * log(...)) instead of exponentiation (10^{...}); correction correctly applies exponentiation for base-10 and natural logs.

problems.quote: i = e ln(A/P)/n – 1
problems.problem: Missing exponentiation: should be e raised to the power (ln(A/P)/n), not e multiplied by ln(A/P)/n.
problems.correction: i = e^{ln(A/P)/n} - 1
problems.verifierReason: Original writes e * ln(A/P)/n (multiplication); correction uses exponentiation e^{ln(A/P)/n} which equals (A/P)^{1/n}, the correct discrete growth factor.

problems.quote: for a premium bond YTM coupon rate.
problems.problem: Incomplete statement; missing comparison between YTM and coupon rate for a premium bond.
problems.correction: for a premium bond YTM is less than the coupon rate
problems.verifierReason: Original fragment missing comparison; correction states correct YTM < coupon for premium bond.

problems.quote: Price = Σ (Coupon × (1 – t_i))/(1+r_post)ᵏ + (Redemption – Price) × (1 – t_c)/(1+r_post)ⁿ
problems.problem: Equation omits return of principal in maturity cash flow; after-tax redemption should include Price plus after-tax capital gain.
problems.correction: Price = Σ (Coupon × (1 – t_i))/(1+r_post)ᵏ + [Price + (Redemption – Price) × (1 – t_c)]/(1+r_post)ⁿ
problems.verifierReason: Original omits principal repayment at maturity; correction includes Price + after-tax capital gain.

problems.quote: When the perpetuity grows at rate g (with g ), the formula is PV = R/(i – g) × (1+i)⁻ᵈ
problems.problem: Missing inequality condition g < i for growing perpetuity formula.
problems.correction: When the perpetuity grows at rate g (with g < i), the formula is PV = R/(i – g) × (1+i)⁻ᵈ
problems.verifierReason: Original missing condition g < i; correction adds necessary convergence condition.

problems.quote: the formula only holds for g , otherwise the present value diverges.
problems.problem: Missing inequality condition g < i.
problems.correction: the formula only holds for g < i, otherwise the present value diverges.
problems.verifierReason: Original incomplete inequality; correction specifies g < i for formula validity.

problems.quote: Distance each travelled: A = 10 km, B = 10 km.
problems.problem: B moves at 5√2 km/h for 2 hours, covering 10√2 km, not 10 km.
problems.correction: Distance each travelled: A = 10 km, B = 10√2 km.
problems.verifierReason: Original B distance 10 km contradicts given speed 5√2 km/h for 2 h; correction 10√2 km is correct.

problems.quote: cos(d/R) = cos(h/R)·cos(R_slant/R) + sin(h/R)·sin(R_slant/R)·cos(α)
problems.problem: The spherical law of cosines is misapplied; h/R and R_slant/R are not central angles on the Earth's surface. The correct relation uses the planar law of cosines in the triangle formed by Earth centre, satellite, and target.
problems.correction: cos(d/R) = ((R+h)² + R² - R_slant²) / (2R(R+h))
problems.verifierReason: Original misapplies spherical law; correct planar law gives cos(d/R)=((R+h)²+R²-R_slant²)/(2R(R+h))

problems.quote: For nadir viewing α = 0, the formula reduces to cos(d/R) = cos((R+h)/R)·cos(R_slant/R) + sin((R+h)/R)·sin(R_slant/R)
problems.problem: (R+h)/R > 1, so its cosine and sine are undefined. The nadir case is the same planar triangle; no separate spherical formula exists.
problems.correction: cos(d/R) = ((R+h)² + R² - R_slant²) / (2R(R+h))
problems.verifierReason: Original uses invalid spherical formula; nadir case uses same planar law as (1)

problems.quote: With R = 6371 km, h = 800 km, R_slant = 1200 km, the ground distance d ≈ 1000 km
problems.problem: The numerical result is incorrect. Using the correct planar law of cosines gives d ≈ 841 km.
problems.correction: d ≈ 841 km
problems.verifierReason: Correct planar law yields d≈843 km; original 1000 km is wrong

problems.quote: dS/dt = (hH / (H - h)²) * (dx/dt)
problems.problem: The derivative of S = hx/(H-h) with respect to time is dS/dt = h/(H-h) * dx/dt, not hH/(H-h)².
problems.correction: dS/dt = (h/(H-h)) * (dx/dt)
problems.verifierReason: Derivative of S=hx/(H-h) w.r.t time is h/(H-h) dx/dt; original has extra H/(H-h)

problems.problem: The computed fused standard deviation is wrong. The correct value is approximately 23.0 m.
problems.verifierReason: Inverse variance fusion gives σ_f≈23.0 m; original 18.5 m miscalculated

problems.quote: freedom of association includes right to form companies
problems.problem: Article 19(1)(c) does not include the right to form companies; a company is not a citizen and cannot claim fundamental rights under Article 19.
problems.correction: freedom of association excludes right to form companies
problems.verifierReason: Article 19(1)(c) guarantees freedom to form associations/unions only to citizens; a company is not a citizen (STC v. CTO, 1963) and the right to incorporate is statutory under Companies Act.

problems.quote: Independent member joining a party after 6 months
problems.problem: Independent members are disqualified immediately upon joining any political party; the 6-month grace period applies only to nominated members.
problems.correction: Independent member joining a party
problems.verifierReason: Tenth Schedule Para 2(2) disqualifies an independent member immediately on joining any party; the 6-month grace period in Para 2(3) applies only to nominated members.

problems.quote: 1/3 of members splitting from party = merger (not defection)
problems.problem: The 1/3 split provision was deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003); now only a merger with 2/3 majority is exempt from defection.
problems.correction: 2/3 of members merging = merger (not defection)
problems.verifierReason: The 1/3 split exemption (old Para 3) was deleted by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003; now only merger with 2/3 majority under Para 4 is exempt from defection.

problems.quote: ₹1 granted to regularise expenditure of a service that is now a government responsibility (after the fact).
problems.problem: Token Grant is for a new service not yet budgeted, not for regularizing past expenditure.
problems.correction: ₹1 granted to enable expenditure on a new service not yet budgeted.
problems.verifierReason: A token grant (₹1) is for a new service not yet budgeted; regularisation of past expenditure requires an Excess Grant under Article 115.

problems.quote: child sultan named Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
problems.problem: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah was an adult, not a child
problems.correction: sultan Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
problems.verifierReason: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah was 18 at accession (born 1298, ruled 1316), not a child

problems.correction: bathing in the Yamuna at Mathura was banned

problems.problem: Earlier mosques existed in India (e.g., Cheraman Juma Mosque)
